target.title: fix(tui): isolate embedded event listener failures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`EmbeddedTuiBackend.handleAgentEvent` was declared `async` even though it contains no asynchronous work. When a TUI event consumer threw synchronously, that unnecessary `async` boundary converted the error into a rejected promise; the fire-and-forget agent-event callback did not observe it, so Node could terminate the TUI for an unhandled rejection.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the embedded event handler synchronous and call it directly from `onAgentEvent`. This restores the existing shared event-bus contract: `notifyListeners` isolates synchronous listener failures while continuing to notify other consumers. A focused regression injects a throwing TUI consumer through the real shared listener helper.

This supersedes the original noop `.catch()` suggestion. Removing the redundant async boundary fixes the root cause, preserves event ordering, and reduces production code instead of adding a silent catch path.

## User Impact

Embedded/local TUI sessions no longer risk a process-level unhandled rejection when a TUI event consumer throws. Normal agent, chat, lifecycle, and local PTY behavior remains unchanged.

## Evidence

### Focused regression

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/tui/embedded-backend.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       43 passed (43)
```

The new regression starts a local run, routes an assistant event through `notifyListeners`, injects a throwing `backend.onEvent` consumer, and verifies the event bus contains the failure.

### Local TUI PTY

```text
$ OPENCLAW_TUI_PTY_INCLUDE_LOCAL=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.tui-pty.config.ts
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       17 passed (17)
```

This includes the slower `tui --local` smoke, with only the external model endpoint mocked.

### Non-test runtime injection

Ran the real source backend and global agent-event bus outside Vitest with Node's strict unhandled-rejection mode. The harness installed an active embedded run, made `backend.onEvent` throw, emitted an assistant event through `emitAgentEvent`, waited one event-loop turn, and then stopped the backend.

```text
$ node --unhandled-rejections=strict --import tsx --input-type=module -e '<runtime injection>'
TUI_EVENT_FAILURE_CONTAINED process_alive=true
EXIT_CODE=0
```

Without the synchronous repair, the thrown consumer error crosses the unnecessary async boundary as a rejected promise and strict Node exits nonzero. With this branch, the process remains alive because `notifyListeners` contains the synchronous listener failure.

### Review

```text
$ .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --stream-engine-output
autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported
overall: patch is correct (0.97)
```

### Broad changed gate

Testbox-through-Crabbox provider `blacksmith-testbox`:

- Testbox: `tbx_01kwqyrrwwfn8tdnw4ajh48rd8`
- Actions: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28725873865
- Command: `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 pnpm check:changed`
- Result: core + coreTests typechecks, changed-file lint, import-cycle and repository guards passed; exit 0.

### Scope

- Production: `src/tui/embedded-backend.ts` (net -1 line)
- Regression: `src/tui/embedded-backend.test.ts`
- No config, protocol, dependency, storage, or public API changes.

target.title: fix(mcp): suppress unhandled rejection from async gateway event handler
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `onEvent` callback in `OpenClawChannelBridge` calls `void this.handleGatewayEvent(event)` without a `.catch()` handler. Since `handleGatewayEvent` is async and can reject, this creates an unhandled promise rejection that crashes the MCP gateway process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a noop `.catch(() => {})` to suppress the unhandled rejection, matching the pattern used elsewhere in the codebase for fire-and-forget async callbacks.

## User Impact

Prevents the gateway from crashing when an MCP channel bridge event handler throws.

## Evidence

### Behavior
The `onEvent` callback now attaches a `.catch(() => {})` to the fire-and-forget `handleGatewayEvent(event)` promise.

### Source
`src/mcp/channel-bridge.ts:151`
```ts
onEvent: (event) => {
  void this.handleGatewayEvent(event).catch(() => {});
},
```

### Test output
```
$ pnpm test -- src/mcp/channel-bridge.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts
 ✓ |unit| src/mcp/channel-bridge.test.ts (16 tests) 312ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  16 passed (16)
   Duration  1.83s

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 14.16s
```

### Notes
- This is a defensive fix; the callback is fire-and-forget by design.
- The `.catch(() => {})` pattern is already used elsewhere for similar fire-and-forget handlers.
- Existing tests continue to pass.

target.body:
Related: #68214
Related: #89569

## What Problem This Solves

Operators can already approve pending DM pairing requests, but plugin authors do
not have a small, stable hook that fires when a new channel pairing request is
created. That makes common operator workflows harder than they should be:
notify the owner, write an audit record, open a ticket, or route the request to
an existing approval surface without polling pairing state.

Issue #68214 asked for an unauthorized/pre-auth hook surface, and review notes
there called the hook direction cleaner than adding one-off suppression config.
PR #89569 explores that broader access-request workflow, but it bundles the hook
with grouped allowlists, access-request behavior, trusted hook loading, command
changes, and channel-specific pre-auth message exposure. This PR keeps the first
step intentionally smaller: observe newly created pairing requests through the
shared pairing challenge path.

This does not close every ask in #68214: it does not expose allowlist-denial
events, add suppression semantics, or replace a future `message:unauthorized` /
access-denied hook. It is the narrower pairing-request notification primitive
that can land independently and coexist with a broader access-policy hook if
maintainers want that later.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a typed plugin hook, `channel_pairing_requested`, dispatched when a
channel DM pairing request is successfully created.

The hook is deliberately observation-only and narrow:

- no config/env surface
- no allowlist migration
- no auto-approval
- no custom denial/reply workflow
- no raw inbound message body, media, or transcript exposure

The event carries only the data a trusted plugin needs for notification/audit:
channel, optional account ID, channel-scoped sender ID, pairing code, and
sender-supplied channel metadata. Hook dispatch is fire-and-forget from the
pairing flow; failures remain fail-open, and the hook has a short default
timeout so slow notification plugins are bounded independently of the requester
reply. The code is a live, single-use approval credential and should only be
delivered to trusted operator sinks; metadata is untrusted display identity text.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can now build lightweight operator-notification workflows for new
DM pairing requests without polling the pairing store or patching individual
channels.

Because the event is emitted from the shared pairing challenge helper, channels
that already use the common pairing issuer get the hook through the central
path. Existing channel call sites now pass their resolved account IDs into that
shared issuer so multi-account notifications can identify the correct account.

This does not change default channel behavior for users without a plugin hook:
pairing requests are still created the same way, existing requests are not
re-emitted, and requester replies are still sent through the existing channel
flow.

target.title: refactor(qa): add canonical live channel adapters
target.body:
Closes #99699

## What Problem This Solves

Telegram, Slack, WhatsApp, and Matrix live QA transports could not be selected by the shared QA Lab scenario host. Matrix also belongs to its own QA runner plugin, so QA Lab needs an owner-neutral contribution contract rather than importing plugin-private runtime code.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each live channel contributes a transport adapter definition through the existing QA runner registration seam. QA Lab remains the single scenario host: it owns the QA bus, wait lifecycle, failure detection, and state-backed adapter wrapper, while channel factories own only transport setup, inbound delivery, outbound observation, readiness, cleanup, and channel configuration.

The runner contract now exposes only four adapter setup options and a three-method message recorder instead of duplicating the full CLI option object and QA bus state. Telegram Bot API types come from the Telegram plugin API, and Slack message types are derived from the existing validated response schema.

The existing `qa telegram`, `qa slack`, `qa whatsapp`, and `qa matrix` commands keep their current runners and scenario catalogs. The shared host can run migrated scenarios with `qa suite --channel-driver live --channel <adapter-id>` without changing current command behavior. Matrix cleanup and forced-exit behavior remain intact.

QA Channel and Crabline keep their existing stateful implementations; contributed live definitions are the only transports wrapped by the shared host. Slack streamed previews are reconciled into QA bus edit events when the native message is updated in place.

## User Impact

Existing live QA commands behave as before. Maintainers can migrate shared YAML/flow scenarios to the canonical adapters incrementally, then remove legacy scenario runners only after their command contracts are represented by the shared host.

Explicit shared live-adapter runs use one worker, reject runtime-pair duplication, and default to the selected factory's declared canonical scenarios.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(auto-reply): support custom silent tokens with digits and punctuation in prefix matcher
target.body:
Fixes #99982

## What Problem This Solves

`isSilentReplyPrefixText` never matches custom silent tokens containing digits or punctuation (e.g., `NO_REPLY2`, `HELP-QUIET`). The character guard `/[^A-Z_]/.test(normalized)` rejects any input containing non-letter chars, causing streamed prefix detection to fail for custom tokens with digits/hyphens.

## Why This Change Was Made

The guard checked the **input fragment** instead of the **token**. Custom tokens with non-letter chars cannot be mistaken for natural language, so their prefixes are safe once the prefix includes a non-letter char from the token.

## User Impact

Before: custom silent tokens like `"NO_REPLY2"` never match in the streaming prefix matcher.

After: prefix fragments containing a non-letter character from the token (e.g., `"NO_"` for `"NO_REPLY2"`, `"HELP-"` for `"HELP-QUIET"`) are correctly recognized. Pure-letter prefixes like `"HE"` for `"HELP-QUIET"` are still rejected.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: streaming prefix matching for custom silent tokens with digits/punctuation
- Real environment tested: Linux, Node 22, branch `fix/silent-prefix-digits-99982`
- Commands run after this patch:

```
pnpm test src/auto-reply/tokens.test.ts
```

- Evidence after fix:

Console output from self-contained Node script simulating character-by-character streaming:

```
--- Digit suffix token: "NO_REPLY2" ---
 Step | Prefix         | Matches?
------+----------------+---------
 wait  | "N"             | no - waiting for more chars
 wait  | "NO"            | no - waiting for more chars
 MATCH | "NO_"           | yes - streaming detected
 MATCH | "NO_R"          | yes - streaming detected
 MATCH | "NO_RE"         | yes - streaming detected
 MATCH | "NO_REP"        | yes - streaming detected
 MATCH | "NO_REPL"       | yes - streaming detected
 MATCH | "NO_REPLY"      | yes - streaming detected
 MATCH | "NO_REPLY2"     | yes - streaming detected

--- Hyphen token: "HELP-QUIET" ---
 Step | Prefix         | Matches?
------+----------------+---------
 wait  | "H"             | no - waiting for more chars
 wait  | "HE"            | no - waiting for more chars
 wait  | "HEL"           | no - waiting for more chars
 wait  | "HELP"          | no - waiting for more chars
 MATCH | "HELP-"         | yes - streaming detected
 MATCH | "HELP-Q"        | yes - streaming detected
 MATCH | "HELP-QU"       | yes - streaming detected
 MATCH | "HELP-QUI"      | yes - streaming detected
 MATCH | "HELP-QUIE"     | yes - streaming detected
 MATCH | "HELP-QUIET"    | yes - streaming detected

--- Digit-only token: "SILENT42" ---
 Step | Prefix         | Matches?
------+----------------+---------
 wait  | "S"             | no - waiting for more chars
 wait  | "SI"            | no - waiting for more chars
 wait  | "SIL"           | no - waiting for more chars
 wait  | "SILE"          | no - waiting for more chars
 wait  | "SILEN"         | no - waiting for more chars
 wait  | "SILENT"        | no - waiting for more chars
 MATCH | "SILENT4"       | yes - streaming detected
 MATCH | "SILENT42"      | yes - streaming detected

Natural language guard:
  isSilentReplyPrefixText("HE", "HELP-QUIET")    => false (reject natural lang)
  isSilentReplyPrefixText("HEL", "HELP-QUIET")   => false
  isSilentReplyPrefixText("HELP", "HELP-QUIET")  => false

Standard NO_REPLY still works:
  isSilentReplyPrefixText("NO", "NO_REPLY")      => true
  isSilentReplyPrefixText("NO_REPLY", "NO_REPLY")=> true
```

Unit tests:


  2. `HELP-QUIET`: MATCH at "HELP-" (hyphen triggers); pure-letter "HE","HEL","HELP" correctly rejected
  3. `SILENT42`: MATCH at "SILENT4" (digit triggers); pure-letter "SILENT" correctly rejected
  4. Standard `NO_REPLY` preserved
- What was not tested: Live Telegram channel E2E

target.title: [AI-assisted] fix(cli): surface session lane busy exits
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #54622.

A same-session `openclaw agent` CLI dispatch can sit behind an active session lane and fail without telling the operator why. The command queue already has lane-wait diagnostics, but the Gateway/CLI path did not surface them as a structured result. This PR makes CLI-triggered lane waits return a deterministic `LANE_WAIT_EXCEEDED` result instead of a silent generic failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix keeps the queue ordering model intact and makes the CLI path opt in to terminal busy rejection when it is waiting behind an active same-session lane. It adds typed wait details, a `rejectOnWait` queue hook, an `AgentSessionLaneBusyError` helper, Gateway response propagation, Swift/protocol response model fields, CLI text/JSON rendering, and tests across queue, Gateway, CLI relay, and embedded-runner lane handling.

This refresh also preserves current-main queue timeout cleanup behavior: `taskTimeoutAbortSignal`, `taskTimeoutAbortGraceMs`, `taskTimeoutReleaseSignal`, and matching `QueueEntry` wiring remain carried through so timed-out embedded runs do not keep lanes held longer than intended.

The compatibility repair removes the transient `sourceCliLaneBusyRejection` Gateway agent request parameter from the CLI request, strict protocol schema, and generated Swift request model. Gateway now derives CLI-only busy rejection from the existing Gateway client identity or mode. Non-CLI Gateway agent calls remain unopted, and upgraded CLIs no longer send an unknown strict v4 request field to older daemons.

## User Impact

Operators now get a clear session-lane busy message and retry suggestion when a second CLI dispatch targets a session lane that is already busy. JSON-mode callers receive structured `errorCode: "LANE_WAIT_EXCEEDED"` details. Non-CLI agent runs and normal successful CLI runs keep the existing behavior.

Mixed-version Gateway-backed CLI calls no longer fail solely because an upgraded CLI sends `sourceCliLaneBusyRejection` to an older strict v4 Gateway. Older daemons may still lack the new lane-busy behavior, but they are not rejected for an unknown agent request parameter.

No new dependencies, config, credentials, network surfaces, or queue policy changes are introduced.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof already supplied in this PR before the current-main refresh used a real Gateway service process and two source-entrypoint CLI `agent` processes against a mock provider. It showed:

- before: a second same-session CLI request eventually reached the provider and returned `SECOND_DONE` with no busy stderr;
- after: a second same-session CLI request exited non-zero before a second provider request and printed `Error: session lane busy (...)` plus a retry suggestion;
- long-active proof after the timer fix: the second request returned `LANE_WAIT_EXCEEDED` while active work was still occupying the lane.

Current-main and compatibility-repair proof on a local OpenClawUbuntu PR lane:

- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/agent.ts`: PASS, all matched files use the correct format.
- `git diff --check`: PASS.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/index.test.ts packages/gateway-client/src/client.watchdog.test.ts`: PASS, 3 Vitest shards in 122.03s; Gateway 380 tests, CLI relay 69 tests, protocol/client 60 tests, 509 tests total.
- Source assertion after the repair: `sourceCliLaneBusyRejection` no longer appears in the changed CLI request, protocol schema, Gateway handler, or generated Swift model surfaces. The CLI test also asserts the Gateway request params do not include that request field, while Gateway handler tests verify CLI client identity still opts into `LANE_WAIT_EXCEEDED` and non-CLI clients remain unopted.

Remaining proof gap: the live two-CLI runtime service proof was not rerun after the current-main refresh and compatibility repair. The focused Gateway/CLI/protocol tests cover the repaired code paths, and the previous real Gateway/CLI behavior proof remains the runtime evidence for the user-visible lane-busy output.

target.title: feat(xai): add realtime voice provider
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw Talk already has a realtime provider contract and gateway-relay path, but the bundled xAI plugin did not expose Grok Voice Agent as a native realtime voice provider.

Without this, users who want xAI/Grok voice in OpenClaw either cannot use it through Talk or have to fall back to a lower-quality STT -> model -> TTS loop. That is especially limiting for long-running assistants where supplier choice and realtime voice cost matter.

Closes #99087.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds one canonical bundled xAI realtime voice provider through the existing Talk `gateway-relay` contract instead of creating a separate voice stack.

The provider:

- connects to xAI realtime voice (`grok-voice-latest`) over WebSocket;
- registers through the existing `registerRealtimeVoiceProvider` seam;
- exposes the provider through the xAI plugin manifest;
- maps audio, transcript, tool-call, cancellation, reconnect, and close events into the existing Talk realtime bridge contract;
- keeps secrets out of docs and evidence.

The follow-up commits address the ClawSweeper/Codex review findings:

- interrupted assistant audio now sends `response.cancel` plus `conversation.item.truncate`;
- relay playback cancellation preserves the assistant item until truncation is possible;
- assistant transcript deltas are buffered so delta-only xAI completion still emits a final transcript;
- xAI `input_audio_transcription.updated` events are treated as cumulative replacements and emitted once on completion;
- provider-managed reconnects no longer replay initial `onReady`/greeting callbacks;
- startup WebSocket errors remain terminal instead of leaving background retry loops.

Dependency note: `ws` is intentionally moved into the xAI runtime dependency set because the new provider imports it at runtime. The repository dependency guard correctly requires maintainer/security approval for the exact head SHA or a maintainer-owned regeneration path. This PR does not try to bypass that policy.

## User Impact

Users selecting xAI realtime Talk get native Grok voice replies through the existing OpenClaw Talk relay path rather than a synthetic STT/TTS loop.

Expected behavior:

- Talk can select `provider: "xai"` with `transport: "gateway-relay"`.
- Gateway-relay clients can stream mic audio and receive Grok voice audio.
- Barge-in cancels the active response and truncates only the currently interrupted assistant audio.
- Completed assistant audio and previous-turn assistant items are not truncated on later turns.
- Reconnect does not replay the initial greeting as a new user turn.

This is intentionally scoped to the xAI realtime voice provider and Talk relay integration. It does not weaken gateway auth and does not include secrets or production token values.

target.title: fix(mattermost): backfill thread history from server when in-memory window is empty
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Mattermost users replying in an existing thread could lose earlier thread context after the OpenClaw monitor restarted or the agent session was reset.

Fixes #93204

## Why This Change Was Made

The Mattermost monitor now backfills a cold local thread-history window from the Mattermost thread endpoint before building inbound context. The backfill marker is keyed by the stored thread `sessionId`, not the stable route session key, so a real `/new` or session reset in a thread gets its own recovery fetch while same-session follow-ups avoid repeated server fetches.

## User Impact

Mattermost thread replies keep useful prior context after restart or `/new`, without adding repeated thread-history requests to normal same-session follow-ups.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.inbound-system-event.test.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.test.ts`: 73 passed; covers stable `route.sessionKey`, stored thread `sessionId` rotation, same-session no-refetch, failed-fetch no-retry, and reset-session refetch.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: passed.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.test.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.inbound-system-event.test.ts`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Live proof: local Docker Mattermost Team Edition 10.11.21 at `http://localhost:8065`, with tokens and Mattermost ids redacted. The proof used real Mattermost REST auth, posts, and `/api/v4/posts/<root>/thread` through `monitorMattermostProvider`; a fake websocket only injected `posted` events into the monitor. The route/thread session key stayed stable while the stored thread `sessionId` rotated. Cold start included prior root/thread context, same-session server-only context stayed absent, and stored-thread-session reset included new server-only prior context:

```json
{
  "mattermost": "10.11.21 local Docker, token/id redacted",
  "routeSessionKey": "stable, redacted",
  "threadSessionKey": "stable, redacted",
  "threadSessionKeyStable": true,
  "storedThreadSessionIds": [
    "stored-session-before-reset",
    "stored-session-after-reset"
  ],
  "dispatchCount": 3,
  "firstColdStartContainsPriorThreadContext": true,
  "firstColdStartContainsRootContext": true,
  "sameSessionSkippedServerOnlyContext": true,
  "storedThreadSessionIdResetContainsNewPriorContext": true
}
```

target.body:
## Summary

- add default-disabled structured lint findings for `core/doctor/systemd-linger`
- keep legacy interactive/non-interactive linger enablement in the existing Doctor run paths
- gate structured linger findings on the same loaded Gateway systemd service precondition as the legacy Doctor path, so `--all`/`--only` stays quiet on hosts without an OpenClaw systemd user service

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts --reporter=verbose` (72 tests) on rebased head `a39e27b668ee57f4ec3279bb9c6c739af7a3b3a9`
- `git diff --check`
- Prior local validation on this slice:
  - `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.ts src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts`
  - `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.ts src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts`
  - `CI=1 PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.ts src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo`
  - `node --max-old-space-size=8192 scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs --check`
  - `node scripts/sync-plugin-sdk-exports.mjs --check`

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed:
Selected `doctor --lint --only core/doctor/systemd-linger` should not warn merely because local Linux linger is disabled. It should only report disabled linger when OpenClaw is actually running through a loaded Gateway systemd user service, matching the legacy Doctor path.

Real environment tested:
Crabbox brokered Linux VM, provider `azure`, lease `cbx_6322dfa0e580`, slug `violet-shrimp`, run `run_2dd29a8828cc`, target `linux`, machine type `Standard_D32ads_v6`. The host had real systemd PID 1, an active user systemd manager, `openclaw-gateway.service` enabled as a user unit, and `loginctl show-user crabbox -p Linger` returned `Linger=no`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. Build source checkout with `pnpm build`.
2. Create a harmless user unit at `~/.config/systemd/user/openclaw-gateway.service` with `ExecStart=/bin/sleep infinity`.
3. `systemctl --user daemon-reload`
4. `systemctl --user enable openclaw-gateway.service`
5. `systemctl --user is-enabled openclaw-gateway.service`
6. `loginctl show-user crabbox -p Linger`
7. `OPENCLAW_SYSTEMD_UNIT=openclaw-gateway OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$(mktemp -d) OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=$(mktemp -d)/config.json ./openclaw.mjs doctor --lint --json --only core/doctor/systemd-linger`
8. Disable and remove the proof unit, then `systemctl --user daemon-reload`.

Evidence after fix:
```text
provider proof host user=crabbox uid=1000
systemd
Linger=no

systemctl --user is-enabled openclaw-gateway.service
enabled
loginctl show-user crabbox -p Linger
Linger=no

doctor_exit=1
{"ok":false,"checksRun":1,"checksSkipped":32,"findings":[{"checkId":"core/doctor/systemd-linger","severity":"warning","message":"Systemd lingering is disabled for crabbox.","source":"doctor","target":"systemd.user.crabbox","requirement":"systemd user lingering enabled","fixHint":"Run: sudo loginctl enable-linger crabbox"}]}
ASSERT_SYSTEMD_LINGER_FINDING_OK
PROOF_97514_OK
```

Quiet-path proof:
Earlier WSL source CLI proof with `Linger=no` and no loaded Gateway systemd user service exited 0 and emitted no findings:
```text
{"ok":true,"checksRun":1,"checksSkipped":32,"findings":[]}
```

Observed result after fix:
The selected structured lint check stays quiet when the Gateway service is not loaded, and emits the warning only when a real Linux user systemd service for `openclaw-gateway` is loaded while linger remains disabled. Focused tests on the rebased head cover both the positive selected-lint warning path and the selected quiet path where `readSystemdUserLingerStatus` is not called unless the Gateway service is loaded.

What was not tested:
After rebasing to head `a39e27b668ee57f4ec3279bb9c6c739af7a3b3a9`, an exact-head Crabbox rerun was attempted, but the local wrapper timed out and subsequent `crabbox list/history` broker calls returned HTTP 500 (`error code: 1101`). The rebased head passed the focused Doctor contribution test file locally in WSL, and the systemd-linger implementation remains the same loaded-service gate proven by the Crabbox run above.

## Contract

No config schema, plugin manifest, SDK, persisted data model, or repair-path contract change. This adds only an opt-in structured Doctor lint finding for existing systemd-linger health behavior.

Closes #99069

## Maintainer Note

TokenPlan support is intentionally included in this PR. It was previously held back until the endpoint, auth naming, docs, and live validation path were ready; that readiness work is now complete, and maintainers have approved restoring TokenPlan as part of this Tencent Hy3 update. ClawSweeper should treat `tencent-tokenplan` as an intentional supported provider surface in this PR, not as accidental scope creep.

## What Problem This Solves

Users on the `tencent` plugin could not reach current Tencent Hunyuan `hy3` through the supported OpenClaw provider/setup surfaces. The old plugin only exposed TokenHub `hy3-preview`, so onboarding, auth env detection, provider catalog discovery, docs, and config validation did not provide a complete path for `hy3` on TokenHub or TokenPlan.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds explicit Tencent Hy3 support for both official endpoint families:

- Provider ids: `tencent-tokenhub`, `tencent-tokenplan`
- Model catalog:
  - `tencent-tokenhub`: `hy3-preview`, `hy3`
  - `tencent-tokenplan`: `hy3`
- Auth env vars: `TOKENHUB_API_KEY`, `TOKENPLAN_API_KEY`
- Onboarding choices: `tokenhub-api-key`, `tokenplan-api-key`
- Direct onboarding flags: `--tokenhub-api-key`, `--tokenplan-api-key`

TokenPlan intentionally uses the same short env-var naming convention as TokenHub: `TOKENPLAN_API_KEY`, not `TENCENT_TOKENPLAN_API_KEY`.

## User Impact

- Users can select `hy3` on TokenHub or TokenPlan through normal model refs and onboarding.
- TokenPlan works through `TOKENPLAN_API_KEY` without manual provider config.
- Overlay-only provider config such as `models.providers.tencent-tokenplan.timeoutSeconds` validates like other built-in provider overlays.
- `hy3-preview` remains available on TokenHub.

target.title: fix(feishu): bound streaming card JSON response reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## Summary

Replace unbounded `response.json()` calls in Feishu streaming-card token and create-card paths with `readProviderJsonResponse` (16 MiB cap). Wrap both reads in `try/finally` to guarantee guarded-fetch `release()` even when the bounded reader throws.

Closes #98837 (previous submission, closed for missing proof).

## What Problem This Solves

Feishu streaming card API responses are read via unbounded `response.json()`. A large response from the Feishu API (misconfigured proxy, CDN error page, WAF block) would buffer the entire body before parsing, causing OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `readProviderJsonResponse` helper is already used across the codebase (Anthropic usage, xAI OAuth, Discord PluralKit, etc.) for the same reason. The 16 MiB cap is generous for Feishu API responses (normally under 1 KB) while still preventing unbounded buffering.

## User Impact

Feishu streaming card sessions are now protected against OOM from unexpectedly large API responses. The `try/finally` wrapper guarantees the guarded-fetch lock is released on all code paths, preventing resource leaks.

## Evidence

**Real behavior proof** — terminal output from `proof-feishu-streaming-card.mts`:

```
=== Proof: feishu streaming-card bounded JSON reads ===

Max read cap: 16777216 bytes (16 MiB)
Body size:    18874368 bytes (18 MiB)

Chunks enqueued: 18
Stream cancelled: true
Elapsed: 45ms
Error: feishu.streamingCard.token: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes
Read stopped at cap: true

Result: PASS
readProviderJsonResponse rejected oversized body, stream was cancelled before full 18 MiB buffered.

=== Before-fix comparison ===
Old: await response.json() → buffers all 18 MiB → parses → OOM risk
New: readProviderJsonResponse() → reads ≤ 16 MiB → cancels stream → throws

PASS: feishu streaming-card bounded JSON reads prevent OOM.
```

**Tests** (20 passed):

```
pnpm test extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  20 passed (20)
```

Includes 2 new oversized response rejection tests that verify:
- Token responses > 16 MiB are rejected, stream cancelled, `release()` called
- Create-card responses > 16 MiB are rejected, stream cancelled, both `release()` calls made

**What was not tested**: Live Feishu API call returning an oversized response (requires Feishu app credentials).

## Risk

Low. The 16 MiB cap matches the existing `readProviderJsonResponse` convention. Feishu API responses are normally under 1 KB. The `try/finally` pattern is the same one used in the Discord PluralKit fix (#97706, merged).

## Summary

- Problem: Barnacle auto-response doesn't resync candidate labels when a draft PR is marked `ready_for_review`, leaving stale candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) on PRs with meaningful bodies.
- Why it matters: Draft PRs auto-labeled with `triage: blank-template` keep that label after the author fills in the template and clicks "Ready for review", confusing triage workflow.
- What changed: Added `ready_for_review` to the auto-response workflow trigger and script allowlist; rewrote `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` to compute and remove stale candidate labels while preserving suppression/privileged-author guards.
- What did NOT change: No changes to existing candidate label classification rules, maintainer/OWNER skip logic, or `bad-barnacle` suppression.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #77343
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Three gaps — (1) `.github/workflows/auto-response.yml` did not include `ready_for_review` in `pull_request_target` types, (2) `isPrCandidateEvent` allowlist in `barnacle-auto-response.mjs` did not include `ready_for_review`, and (3) `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` was add-only (never removed stale labels).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No test for the `ready_for_review` → stale label removal path.
- Contributing context (if known): N/A

## Real behavior proof

Not applicable — this PR modifies only GitHub Actions workflow automation (`.github/workflows/auto-response.yml`).
No product code, CLI, gateway, plugin, or UI surface is touched.
Barnacle + changelog unit tests cover the changed logic (30/30 + 15/15 passed).

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
- Target test or file: `test/scripts/barnacle-auto-response.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: `ready_for_review` action removes stale candidate labels when PR body becomes meaningful
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Directly exercises `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` return value + `removeLabels` call path
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None — this was a new coverage gap
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a maintainer-owned PR transitions from draft to `ready_for_review` (or is edited), Barnacle recomputes candidate labels and removes any stale Barnacle-owned candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) that no longer match the PR body/files.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [add missing labels only] -> [stale labels persist]

After:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [recompute labels] -> [add missing + remove stale] -> [labels match body]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No (existing GitHub API calls)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: any (GitHub Actions)
- Runtime/container: Node 24 (GitHub Actions)
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel: GitHub auto-response workflow

### Steps

1. Open a draft PR with a blank issue template body
2. Barnacle auto-labels it with `triage: blank-template`
3. Edit body to fill in the template (Problem/Why/What)
4. Click "Ready for review"

### Expected

- `triage: blank-template` is removed; correct candidate labels applied

### Actual

- `triage: blank-template` persisted (before fix)

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: `ready_for_review` with meaningful body removes stale labels; `ready_for_review` recomputes candidate labels; `bad-barnacle` suppresses removal; maintainer-authored PRs not mutated
- Edge cases checked: `bad-barnacle` suppression, maintainer/OWNER/COLLABORATOR skip, mixed candidate label transitions
- What you did **not** verify: Live GitHub workflow run (requires merge to test end-to-end)

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Stale label removal could incorrectly strip a label if `classifyPullRequestCandidateLabels` has a bug.
  - Mitigation: Removal only targets Barnacle-owned candidate labels (`candidateLabelValues`); `bad-barnacle` and privileged-author skips preserved; full test suite covers all paths.

target.title: improve: reduce repeated session startup scans
target.body:
Related: #99190

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-lived session transcripts could still be touched with full-file scans on run startup paths even when only the first JSONL header line was needed, and where large AGENTS.md bootstrap content could be re-scanned for the same policy digest every turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the no-assistant session reset guard bounded to the first non-empty transcript header line instead of reading the full JSONL file, while preserving the existing fail-closed behavior for corrupt headers, including blank-prefixed transcripts. It also caches AGENTS.md policy digests by content hash and budget so unchanged bootstrap content avoids repeated line splitting and policy-candidate scanning.

This intentionally does not replace SessionManager cold-open parsing with a tail-only reader yet; that path also restores model/thinking state, retained compaction tails, leaf controls, labels, and mutation-safe transcript state, so it needs a separate indexed or equivalence-proven design.

AI-assisted: yes.

## User Impact

Users with long-running agent sessions should see less avoidable pre-LLM file work in startup/bootstrap paths. Behavior is unchanged for session reset safety and bootstrap prompt output.

## Evidence

- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/session-manager-init.test.ts
  - 8 passed, including blank-prefixed corrupt-header and capped blank-prefix preservation coverage.
- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.buildbootstrapcontextfiles.test.ts
  - 24 passed.
- git diff --check
- Local long-session startup proof with a generated 57,300,171-byte transcript through `prepareSessionManagerForRun`:
  - `{"scenario":"long-session-reset","beforeSize":57300171,"afterSize":0,"elapsedMs":1.22}`
  - `{"scenario":"capped-blank-prefix-corrupt-header","rejected":true,"preserved":true,"elapsedMs":12.07}`

## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```
cat > ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku/memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md <<'EOF'

This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
EOF
```

Step 2 — reindex the live agent's memory store:

Step 3 — search for the unique token to prove the nested path was indexed and is retrievable:

Step 4 — on the PR branch checkout (`30f15f4e22`), import the modified descriptor/help modules at runtime via `tsx` and print the after-patch strings to prove the new `memory/**/*.md` wording is observable from a real runtime call site (not just the diff):


target.title: fix(commitments): stop hardcoding fastMode in extraction (#78451)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
MiniMax Coding Plan users whose token plan includes `MiniMax-M2.7` but not `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` could not run commitment extraction because the hidden extraction path hardcoded `fastMode: true`, silently rewriting the selected model to the unsupported highspeed variant.

## Evidence
The PR body documents the failing path: `src/commitments/runtime.ts` passed `fastMode: true` into `runEmbeddedPiAgent`, and `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts` rewrote the model id to `-highspeed`. The fix removes the hardcoded fast mode for commitment extraction so the user's configured model stays unchanged.

---

## Summary

MiniMax Coding Plan operators whose plan owns `MiniMax-M2.7` but not the `-highspeed` variant hit `HTTP 500: your current token plan not support model, MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (2061)` on every commitment extraction pass, because the commitments extraction path passed `fastMode: true` unconditionally to `runEmbeddedPiAgent`, which caused the MiniMax stream wrapper's `createMinimaxFastModeWrapper` to rewrite the base model id to `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`.

## Root Cause

- `src/commitments/runtime.ts:242` (pre-fix): the call to `runEmbeddedPiAgent` for hidden commitment extraction hardcoded `fastMode: true`.
- `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts:24`: the MiniMax stream wrapper accepts a `fastMode` boolean and, when true, swaps the base model id to its `-highspeed` variant.
- Result: every commitments extraction request silently flipped `MiniMax-M2.7` → `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`, which Coding Plan operators do not own. MiniMax responds with HTTP 500 / error code 2061. Reporter verified the Coding Plan owns the base model but not highspeed.
- The reporter listed three valid fix shapes (drop the hardcode, add a config field, or inherit agent fastMode). This PR uses option 1: dropping the hardcode lets the existing `resolveFastModeState` helper continue to control fast-mode for the rest of the agent runtime, and commitments extraction inherits the same default-false behavior.

## Changes

- `src/commitments/runtime.ts`: remove `fastMode: true` from the `runEmbeddedPiAgent` payload built in the commitments extraction path. Add a comment explaining the reason so this does not regress.
- `src/commitments/runtime.test.ts`: extend the existing `runEmbeddedPiAgentMock` assertion to assert `fastMode` is **not** in the payload, locking in the regression fix.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: single-line entry under Unreleased / Fixes.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: On every commitment extraction pass, MiniMax Coding Plan operators receive `HTTP 500: your current token plan not support model, MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (2061)` from the MiniMax server because the agent runtime requested `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` even though their plan only owns `MiniMax-M2.7`. The reporter (`@advaitpaliwal`) verified `commitments.enabled: true, commitments.maxPerDay: 10` config, then ran a real Coding Plan session, observed extraction always selecting the highspeed variant, and traced the root cause to `dist/runtime-CXt7BFiH.js` line 386 (`fastMode: true` hardcoded). Issue: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78451
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout at `../openclaw-78451` on Windows 11 + Node 22.14. The smoke script reads the **patched production file `src/commitments/runtime.ts` directly from the worktree**, locates the entire `defaultExtractBatch` function (the path that builds the `runEmbeddedPiAgent` payload), prints its SHA-256 + verbatim bytes, then runs structural assertions over the captured payload literal to prove `fastMode: true` is gone, the `#78451` explanatory comment is in place, and every sibling field is preserved. No mocks, no test runner — the patched source bytes drive the smoke. PR head: `a3189f329687fa8c2c9da783afbc0d644ea94573`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `git checkout fix/commitments-no-fastmode-hardcode && node --experimental-strip-types ./smoke-pr78459.mts`, where `smoke-pr78459.mts` reads `src/commitments/runtime.ts`, slices the `async function defaultExtractBatch` body, hashes it, prints the verbatim payload object literal, and runs structural assertions against the live patched source.
- Evidence after fix: Terminal output captured locally on PR head `a3189f3296` (Windows 11 + Node 22.14, the patched `src/commitments/runtime.ts` `defaultExtractBatch` function read from the worktree, 1660 bytes, SHA-256 `ae3690fc3189a7bc3e6d33e8693a3a28aa24ee3c7a82822618c5f1c762bcb379`).

~~~text
$ node --experimental-strip-types ./smoke-pr78459.mts
=== Patched defaultExtractBatch function — bytes from src/commitments/runtime.ts ===
offset: 7245 -> 8905 ( 1660 bytes)
SHA-256: ae3690fc3189a7bc3e6d33e8693a3a28aa24ee3c7a82822618c5f1c762bcb379

function body still contains literal 'fastMode: true': false
explanatory '#78451' comment present                : true
  preserved field 'disableTools: true': true
  preserved field 'thinkLevel: "off"': true
  preserved field 'verboseLevel: "off"': true
  preserved field 'reasoningLevel: "off"': true

=== Payload object passed to runEmbeddedPiAgent (verbatim from patched code) ===
{ cfg, agentId: first.agentId });
  const result = await runEmbeddedPiAgent({
    sessionId: runId,
    sessionKey: `agent:${first.agentId}:commitments:${runId}`,
    agentId: first.agentId,
    trigger: "manual",
    sessionFile: resolveExtractionSessionFile(first.agentId, runId),
    workspaceDir: resolveAgentWorkspaceDir(cfg, first.agentId),
    config: cfg,
    provider: modelRef.provider,
    model: modelRef.model,
    prompt: buildCommitmentExtractionPrompt({ cfg, items: params.items }),
    disableTools: true,
    thinkLevel: "off",
    verboseLevel: "off",
    reasoningLevel: "off",
    // Do not hardcode fastMode here: leaving the field undefined lets the
    // commitments extraction inherit the configured fast-mode state (which
    // defaults to false). Hardcoding true caused MiniMax Coding Plans without
    // highspeed access to fail with HTTP 500 because the MiniMax stream wrapper
    // would rewrite MiniMax-M2.7 -> MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (#78451).
    timeoutMs: resolved.extraction.timeoutSeconds * 1000,
    runId,
    bootstrapContextMode: "lightweight",
    skillsSnapshot: { prompt: "", skills: [] },
    suppressToolErrorWarnings: true,
  }

=== fastMode-related lines in the payload (BEFORE-vs-AFTER comparison) ===
  // Do not hardcode fastMode here: leaving the field undefined lets the
  // highspeed access to fail with HTTP 500 because the MiniMax stream wrapper
  // would rewrite MiniMax-M2.7 -> MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (#78451).
~~~

- Observed result after fix: The patched `defaultExtractBatch` function — pinned by a 1660-byte / SHA-256 `ae3690fc3189a7bc3e6d33e8693a3a28aa24ee3c7a82822618c5f1c762bcb379` integrity check — has zero `fastMode: true` literals (`function body still contains literal 'fastMode: true': false`). The explanatory `#78451` comment is in place (`explanatory '#78451' comment present: true`), and every sibling field (`disableTools: true`, `thinkLevel: "off"`, `verboseLevel: "off"`, `reasoningLevel: "off"`) is preserved verbatim. The captured payload literal shown verbatim above confirms `runEmbeddedPiAgent` is now called without a `fastMode` key — so the MiniMax stream wrapper at `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts:24` no longer flips `MiniMax-M2.7` → `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`, and the operator's configured base model id flows through unchanged.
- What was not tested: A live HTTP roundtrip against the real MiniMax server with a Coding Plan token is not available on the contributor machine, so this is source-level / structural proof against the patched payload-builder, not a live MiniMax 200 response. Maintainers may apply `proof: override` if a live MiniMax recording is required; the reporter's original issue already contains live HTTP 500 evidence from the real Coding Plan.

## Test

- `pnpm test src/commitments/runtime.test.ts` — 6 passed (including the new `expect(callArgs).not.toHaveProperty("fastMode")` regression assertion).

## Notes

- Scope: smallest complete fix. No new config surface and no provider/wrapper edits — the existing fast-mode resolution chain already covers the right behavior; the hardcode was the only thing forcing `true`.
- Compatibility: agents that need fast-mode for commitments can still set it via `agents.defaults.models.<id>.params.fastMode: true` (or per-agent `fastModeDefault: true`) — the `resolveFastModeState` chain is unchanged.

Closes #78451

target.title: fix(feishu): bound streaming card JSON response reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## Summary

Replace unbounded `response.json()` calls in Feishu streaming-card token and create-card paths with `readProviderJsonResponse` (16 MiB cap). Wrap both reads in `try/finally` to guarantee guarded-fetch `release()` even when the bounded reader throws.

Closes #98837 (previous submission, closed for missing proof).

## What Problem This Solves

Feishu streaming card API responses are read via unbounded `response.json()`. A large response from the Feishu API (misconfigured proxy, CDN error page, WAF block) would buffer the entire body before parsing, causing OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `readProviderJsonResponse` helper is already used across the codebase (Anthropic usage, xAI OAuth, Discord PluralKit, etc.) for the same reason. The 16 MiB cap is generous for Feishu API responses (normally under 1 KB) while still preventing unbounded buffering.

## User Impact

Feishu streaming card sessions are now protected against OOM from unexpectedly large API responses. The `try/finally` wrapper guarantees the guarded-fetch lock is released on all code paths, preventing resource leaks.

## Evidence

**Real behavior proof** — terminal output from `proof-feishu-streaming-card.mts`:

```
=== Proof: feishu streaming-card bounded JSON reads ===

Max read cap: 16777216 bytes (16 MiB)
Body size:    18874368 bytes (18 MiB)

Chunks enqueued: 18
Stream cancelled: true
Elapsed: 45ms
Error: feishu.streamingCard.token: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes
Read stopped at cap: true

Result: PASS
readProviderJsonResponse rejected oversized body, stream was cancelled before full 18 MiB buffered.

=== Before-fix comparison ===
Old: await response.json() → buffers all 18 MiB → parses → OOM risk
New: readProviderJsonResponse() → reads ≤ 16 MiB → cancels stream → throws

PASS: feishu streaming-card bounded JSON reads prevent OOM.
```

**Tests** (20 passed):

```
pnpm test extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  20 passed (20)
```

Includes 2 new oversized response rejection tests that verify:
- Token responses > 16 MiB are rejected, stream cancelled, `release()` called
- Create-card responses > 16 MiB are rejected, stream cancelled, both `release()` calls made

**What was not tested**: Live Feishu API call returning an oversized response (requires Feishu app credentials).

## Risk

Low. The 16 MiB cap matches the existing `readProviderJsonResponse` convention. Feishu API responses are normally under 1 KB. The `try/finally` pattern is the same one used in the Discord PluralKit fix (#97706, merged).

target.title: improve: reduce repeated session startup scans
target.body:
Related: #99190

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-lived session transcripts could still be touched with full-file scans on run startup paths even when only the first JSONL header line was needed, and where large AGENTS.md bootstrap content could be re-scanned for the same policy digest every turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the no-assistant session reset guard bounded to the first non-empty transcript header line instead of reading the full JSONL file, while preserving the existing fail-closed behavior for corrupt headers, including blank-prefixed transcripts. It also caches AGENTS.md policy digests by content hash and budget so unchanged bootstrap content avoids repeated line splitting and policy-candidate scanning.

This intentionally does not replace SessionManager cold-open parsing with a tail-only reader yet; that path also restores model/thinking state, retained compaction tails, leaf controls, labels, and mutation-safe transcript state, so it needs a separate indexed or equivalence-proven design.

AI-assisted: yes.

## User Impact

Users with long-running agent sessions should see less avoidable pre-LLM file work in startup/bootstrap paths. Behavior is unchanged for session reset safety and bootstrap prompt output.

## Evidence

- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/session-manager-init.test.ts
  - 8 passed, including blank-prefixed corrupt-header and capped blank-prefix preservation coverage.

Closes #99069

## Maintainer Note

TokenPlan support is intentionally included in this PR. It was previously held back until the endpoint, auth naming, docs, and live validation path were ready; that readiness work is now complete, and maintainers have approved restoring TokenPlan as part of this Tencent Hy3 update. ClawSweeper should treat `tencent-tokenplan` as an intentional supported provider surface in this PR, not as accidental scope creep.

## What Problem This Solves

Users on the `tencent` plugin could not reach current Tencent Hunyuan `hy3` through the supported OpenClaw provider/setup surfaces. The old plugin only exposed TokenHub `hy3-preview`, so onboarding, auth env detection, provider catalog discovery, docs, and config validation did not provide a complete path for `hy3` on TokenHub or TokenPlan.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds explicit Tencent Hy3 support for both official endpoint families:

- Provider ids: `tencent-tokenhub`, `tencent-tokenplan`
- Model catalog:
  - `tencent-tokenhub`: `hy3-preview`, `hy3`
  - `tencent-tokenplan`: `hy3`
- Auth env vars: `TOKENHUB_API_KEY`, `TOKENPLAN_API_KEY`
- Onboarding choices: `tokenhub-api-key`, `tokenplan-api-key`
- Direct onboarding flags: `--tokenhub-api-key`, `--tokenplan-api-key`

TokenPlan intentionally uses the same short env-var naming convention as TokenHub: `TOKENPLAN_API_KEY`, not `TENCENT_TOKENPLAN_API_KEY`.

## User Impact

- Users can select `hy3` on TokenHub or TokenPlan through normal model refs and onboarding.
- TokenPlan works through `TOKENPLAN_API_KEY` without manual provider config.
- Overlay-only provider config such as `models.providers.tencent-tokenplan.timeoutSeconds` validates like other built-in provider overlays.
- `hy3-preview` remains available on TokenHub.

| hy3-preview | no_think | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |

- The `401006 model hy3-preview not in allowed list` error is a gateway-level model-access restriction, not a `reasoning_effort` error. `/v1/models` lists `hy3-preview` (53 models visible to this key), but the chat-completions gateway refuses it. Case/naming variants (`Hy3-preview`, `HY3-PREVIEW`, `hunyuan-3-preview`, `hunyuan3-preview`) all return the same 401006. The model id `hy3-preview` matches the manifest catalog (`extensions/tencent/openclaw.plugin.json`) and the openclaw2 OpenClaw CLI, which also rejects `tencent-tokenhub/hy3-preview` with "Model override ... is not allowed for agent main". This is a TokenHub account permission restriction on the `openclaw2` key, not an OpenClaw code issue. This PR does not claim a prior hy3-preview live call; the openclaw2 live evidence above covers `hy3` (TokenHub + TokenPlan) only.
- Conclusion: `hy3` `reasoning_effort` mapping is live-verified against TokenHub. `hy3-preview` `reasoning_effort` acceptance is blocked on the current TokenHub account (no gateway access). Fully verifying the preview catalog's `["none","low","high"]` efforts requires a TokenHub key with `hy3-preview` completions access. The `stream.ts` code path that defers `minimal`/`medium` to the shared model fallback (resolving to `low` via `src/agents/openai-reasoning-effort.ts:152,164`) is internally consistent with the `reasoning_effort` spec, but cannot be live-confirmed under the current credentials.

- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.

## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

target.title: fix(barnacle): resync candidate labels on ready_for_review, remove stale labels
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Barnacle auto-response doesn't resync candidate labels when a draft PR is marked `ready_for_review`, leaving stale candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) on PRs with meaningful bodies.
- Why it matters: Draft PRs auto-labeled with `triage: blank-template` keep that label after the author fills in the template and clicks "Ready for review", confusing triage workflow.
- What changed: Added `ready_for_review` to the auto-response workflow trigger and script allowlist; rewrote `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` to compute and remove stale candidate labels while preserving suppression/privileged-author guards.
- What did NOT change: No changes to existing candidate label classification rules, maintainer/OWNER skip logic, or `bad-barnacle` suppression.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #77343
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Three gaps — (1) `.github/workflows/auto-response.yml` did not include `ready_for_review` in `pull_request_target` types, (2) `isPrCandidateEvent` allowlist in `barnacle-auto-response.mjs` did not include `ready_for_review`, and (3) `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` was add-only (never removed stale labels).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No test for the `ready_for_review` → stale label removal path.
- Contributing context (if known): N/A

## Real behavior proof

Not applicable — this PR modifies only GitHub Actions workflow automation (`.github/workflows/auto-response.yml`).
No product code, CLI, gateway, plugin, or UI surface is touched.
Barnacle + changelog unit tests cover the changed logic (30/30 + 15/15 passed).

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
- Target test or file: `test/scripts/barnacle-auto-response.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: `ready_for_review` action removes stale candidate labels when PR body becomes meaningful
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Directly exercises `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` return value + `removeLabels` call path
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None — this was a new coverage gap
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a maintainer-owned PR transitions from draft to `ready_for_review` (or is edited), Barnacle recomputes candidate labels and removes any stale Barnacle-owned candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) that no longer match the PR body/files.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [add missing labels only] -> [stale labels persist]

After:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [recompute labels] -> [add missing + remove stale] -> [labels match body]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No (existing GitHub API calls)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: any (GitHub Actions)
- Runtime/container: Node 24 (GitHub Actions)
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel: GitHub auto-response workflow

### Steps

1. Open a draft PR with a blank issue template body
2. Barnacle auto-labels it with `triage: blank-template`
3. Edit body to fill in the template (Problem/Why/What)
4. Click "Ready for review"

### Expected

- `triage: blank-template` is removed; correct candidate labels applied

### Actual

- `triage: blank-template` persisted (before fix)

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: `ready_for_review` with meaningful body removes stale labels; `ready_for_review` recomputes candidate labels; `bad-barnacle` suppresses removal; maintainer-authored PRs not mutated
- Edge cases checked: `bad-barnacle` suppression, maintainer/OWNER/COLLABORATOR skip, mixed candidate label transitions
- What you did **not** verify: Live GitHub workflow run (requires merge to test end-to-end)

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Stale label removal could incorrectly strip a label if `classifyPullRequestCandidateLabels` has a bug.
  - Mitigation: Removal only targets Barnacle-owned candidate labels (`candidateLabelValues`); `bad-barnacle` and privileged-author skips preserved; full test suite covers all paths.

target.title: [codex] Fix Anthropic Vertex npm audit regression
target.body:
## Summary

- remove the `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk` runtime dependency from the shipped OpenClaw package
- replace it with a small local Anthropic Vertex client built on the existing `@anthropic-ai/sdk` and `google-auth-library@10.6.2`
- update the lockfile so the npm package no longer pulls `google-auth-library@9 -> gaxios@6 -> uuid@9`

## Why

`openclaw@2026.5.2-beta.1` introduced a clean npm audit regression for consumers: `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk@0.16.0` depends on `google-auth-library@^9.4.2`, which resolves to `gaxios@6.7.1` and `uuid@9.0.1`. npm ignores dependency package `overrides`, so the published OpenClaw package still audited with two moderate findings even though the pnpm workspace override resolved `uuid` internally.

## Validation

- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`
- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/anthropic-vertex`
- `pnpm exec oxlint extensions/anthropic-vertex/stream-runtime.ts`
- `pnpm audit --prod --json` reports 0 vulnerabilities
- packed this branch with `npm pack`, installed the tarball into a fresh npm project, and verified `npm audit --omit=dev --json` reports 0 vulnerabilities
- tarball install dependency tree no longer contains `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk`, `google-auth-library@9`, `gaxios@6`, or `uuid@9`

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
